questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why many South Koreans get so little sleep
How to set a world record for staying awake
Why afternoon naps are bad for your health
How South Korean companies became so successful
questions.why: Sam says South Korea is one of the most stressed and tired nations, where people get less sleep than anywhere.

questions.q: What do Sam and Neil say about their own sleep?
options: Both need at least ten hours a night
Neil takes naps, but Sam never does
Sam likes a nap; Neil falls asleep fast
Both of them find it hard to fall asleep
questions.why: Sam gets by on seven hours and likes an afternoon nap; Neil says he's 'out like a light'.

questions.q: What does research show about people in South Korea?
options: They sleep more than people in most countries
They sleep less and are often depressed
They work fewer hours than people in Europe
They find it easy to stop thinking about work
questions.why: Neil says South Koreans sleep fewer hours and have higher rates of depression and suicide than almost anywhere.

questions.q: What did Ji-an's employer expect from her?
options: To work only from home at night
To take a nap at a sleep cafe every day
To stop contacting colleagues after work
To be ready to answer work contact 24/7
questions.why: She says, 'They told me you need to be contactable 24/7.'

questions.q: How does Ji-an feel when she thinks about her old job?
options: Very upset and worried
Proud of how hard she worked
Bored and a little sleepy
Happy that she was needed
questions.why: She says, 'Even just thinking about it, I get really agitated.'

questions.q: What businesses have grown because of sleeplessness in South Korea?
options: Late-night restaurants and bars
Shops selling expensive new beds
Sleep clinics and cafes for naps
Coffee shops that open all night
questions.why: Sam says there are sleep clinics that assess people overnight, and sleep cafes to nap during the day.

options: A tradition of taking long lunch breaks
A habit of drinking tea before bed
A way of relaxing through meditation
People always being in a hurry
questions.why: Neil says it means 'quickly, quickly' or 'hurry, hurry' – people are constantly in a rush.

questions.q: According to Dr Lee, what problems do some sleeping pill users have?
options: They stop feeling tired during the day
They sleepwalk and do things they forget
They sleep for more than twenty hours
They become much more relaxed at work
questions.why: He says people can sleepwalk, eat uncooked food and not remember it next day; some even cause car accidents.
